answer: Require each agent to post a small refundable bond before trading, tied to a persistent identity whose reputation grows only through completed work. Like a vine that strengthens as it climbs, trust accumulates slowly and cannot be bought instantly. A newcomer faces strict rate limits, while a ferrous record of verified transactions makes its history hard to forge. An attacker spawning many fakes must fund every bond and wait out the slow ramp, facing slashing for cheating, so cost scales per fake while honest agents pay once, and a zephyr of cheap accounts cannot overwhelm the market.
